findings.cross_file_justification: floor.yaml declares 16 fence:* rows as floor guards; those fences are implemented in .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh (touched in this diff), which is not listed in floor_files.
findings.description: The floor header states these guards may not be weakened by any cycle task, and floor-snapshot.bats enforces that by pinning floor_files bytes. All 16 fence floor rows (FR-1.2b, FR-SZ*, FR-SZ2*) live in block-destructive-bash.sh, but only the corpus rows are pinned, not the hook. A cycle task can edit the hook (e.g. add an early return or widen an allow-list) and the floor snapshot passes as long as the corpus fixture bytes do not change; the corpus replay only catches weakenings its existing rows happen to exercise. The gate and policy floor rows do pin their implementing scripts (verdict-derive.sh, adversarial-review-gate.sh, settings.deny.json), so the fence rows are protected inconsistently.
findings.failure_mode: A weakening of FR-SZ/FR-SZ2 protection that passes the current corpus is not detected by the floor test, contradicting the documented floor guarantee.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add block-destructive-bash.sh to floor_files (and accept that fence edits require a deliberate floor-pin update, as this very diff would), or document explicitly in floor.yaml that fence rows are protected only via floor_corpus and require the corpus to be run with LOA_ALLOW_STATE_ZONE_EXEC_WRITE unset and no marker present.

findings.cross_file_justification: The template comment states the ⇐ blockers segment is parsed into the bead --deps flag; the parser lives outside this diff and now receives a trailing ' · kind: <token>' after the blockers.
findings.description: The kind token is appended after the ⇐ blockers segment, which the template itself documents as machine-parsed into --deps ('edge-or-none rule'). If the deps extractor takes everything after ⇐ to end of line, 'none · kind: mechanical' no longer equals 'none' and 'Task 1.1 · kind: judgment' is not a task id. The visible diff does not show the parser or a test covering a task line with both ⇐ and kind.
findings.failure_mode: Bead creation from a new sprint plan fails or produces a bogus dependency edge for every task line, breaking the executable DAG.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify the --deps extractor (sprint-plan bead creation script) tolerates the trailing ' · kind: …' segment and add a bats case for '⇐ none · kind: mechanical' and '⇐ Task 1.1 · kind: judgment'. Alternatively place the kind token before the → goal refs so the ⇐ segment stays last.

findings.description: The implementing-tasks skill's declared App-zone permission is widened from read to read-write in a diff otherwise about the guard register and floor. The visible diff contains no rationale, no test, and no corresponding change in skill-invariants.md (which this diff edits and which describes zones as the path-level barrier). Implementation does need App writes, so this may be a correctness fix, but it silently removes the confirmation-before-write posture the Zone glossary entry describes.
findings.failure_mode: If any validator or gate reads the skill's zones.app permission to decide whether to prompt, App writes under /implement stop prompting without an explicit decision record.
findings.suggested_fix: Either revert to read, or add the rationale (DEC row / sprint task) and confirm no reader of zones.app treats read-write as skip-confirmation; check validate-skill-capabilities.sh and implement-gate.sh.

findings.description: Adding a paths: frontmatter makes this rule conditionally loaded only when the model reads or edits *.sh, *.bats, .claude/scripts or .claude/hooks files. The rule governs git stash commands issued through Bash, which do not touch any such file. A session that runs 'git stash push | tail -1' without editing a shell script never loads the rule. The mechanical fence FR-1.2b still catches the swallowed-output shapes, but the prose guard is narrowed with no note in the rule body.
findings.failure_mode: The stash-safety prose guard is absent in exactly the sessions where stash misuse is most likely (pure Bash workflows), leaving only the regex fence.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop paths: for this rule so it stays always-on, or widen it to include the files commonly edited during git work, and record the scoping decision in the rule body.
